TOP NEWS "Parole decision reached for Selena's killer Yolanda Saldivar, " San Antonio Express-News' Gabriella Ybarra andNancy M. Preyor-Johnson -- "Yolanda Sald ivar, the convicted killer of Tejano music icon Selena Quintanilla-Perez , will remain in prison, the state's parole board announced. The decision came Thursday, after the Texas Board of Pardons and Paroles voted to deny the release of Saldivar -- who has been serving a life sentence at the Patrick O'Daniel Unit prison in Gatesville -- for fatally shooting Selena on March 31, 1995, in Corpus Christi. Saldivar, a native of San Antonio, was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison on Oct. 26, 1995. She was required to serve 30 years before becoming eligible for parole consideration. Her parole eligibility date was set for March 30. According to a statement from the parole board, the parole review process began about six months before her parole eligibility date A parole officer prepared the case summary file to submit to the parole board voting panel. "Within that confidential file, there is a plethora of information including but not limited to court documents, offense reports, support/protest information, criminal history, institutional adjustment, and information/statements provided by the offender," the statement continued. "The file was then sent to a parole panel of three. A simple majority was required to either grant or deny parole." After considering all available information, including confidential interviews, the panel denied Saldivar, 64, parole. The reason cited by the panel for denial was the "nature of the offense." "The record indicates that the instant offense has elements of brutality, violence, assaultive behavior or conscious selection of victim's vulnerability indicating a conscious disregard for the lives, safety, or property of others, such that the offender poses a continuing threat to public safety," the statement read. Recently, Saldivar's family said Saldivar believes Selena was at least partly at fault because she was "forceful" in confronting Saldivar about allegedly embezzling funds. Selena, known as the "Queen of Tejano," was 23 years old when she was killed after meeting with then 32-year-old Saldivar at the Days Inn hotel in Corpus Christi to retrieve financial records." ($) #TXLEGE " Health care CEO fired after Texas House DOGE hearing," Dallas Morning News'Karen Brooks Harper and Nolan D. McCaskill -- "The chief executive of a private health insurance company who admitted in a legislative hearing Wednesday to hiring private investigators to spy on customers has been fired. The dismissal of Superior HealthPlan CEO Mark Sanders follows his testimony Wednesday to the Texas House Delivery of Government Efficiency Committee in a hearing on Medicaid procurement, during which he acknowledged hiring private investigators to get background information on lawmakers and others. "The conduct highlighted yesterday during the course of the Texas House Committee hearing is not reflective of our values nor is it a practice Centene's current leadership condones," Centene, Superior's parent company, said in a statement to The Dallas Morning News. "To this end, Mark Sanders is no longer with our organization." Sanders' termination comes hours after Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton announced he was investigating the company over the allegations aired inside the Capitol on Wednesday. "The allegations concerning Superior's actions, such as actions that were characterized as potentially blackmailing lawmakers to secure state contracts and surveilling private citizens to avoid paying legitimate claims, are deeply troubling," Paxton said in a statement. "I will get to the bottom of this, uncover any illegal activity, and hold bad actors responsible." At the center of the probe is a series of private investigations, starting in 2017 and allegedly ordered by Sanders, who had just taken the helm as chief executive officer of Superior. The health care firm was facing lawsuits at the time over declining coverage. Sanders, who headed one of the state's biggest providers of health insurance for children on Medicaid, told lawmakers under questioning Wednesday that investigators had done "routine" background checks into several state representatives, senators, health care providers, patients and their families, and a journalist several years ago. The company has abandoned that practice, Sanders told the committee during a tense hearing he acknowledged was "rough" for him. "We've done what I would call general research," Sanders said. "Anything that's publicly available." Centene said it regretted the impact Sanders' conduct has had on the company's partners. "Superior's credibility rests on being a trusted partner to our members, government stakeholders and providers," Centene said. "While we took the necessary steps to ensure this conduct was stopped a number of years ago, yesterday's hearing made clear we failed to address its full impact." "We are committed to building transparent and trusted relationships with our government partners and remain focused on our mission to improve the health and well-being of the Texas communities we serve," the statement added. The subjects of those investigations included Texas Land Commissioner Dawn Buckingham , then a state senator, and Southlake Republican state Rep. Giovanni Capriglione , according to documents obtained by The Dallas Morning News. "You've hired private investigators to look at not only but also people who have filed claims and felt that they deserved those claims but that you felt that they didn't," Capriglione, chairman of the DOGE committee, said at Wednesday's hearing. "You were doing that for what purpose?" he asked. "Why would you go and run a background check, hire a private investigator to follow, to dig into the records of people who are your customers?" In an interview Thursday, Capriglione said while it was good Sanders is no longer with the company, Paxton's investigation should proceed. "When this happens, it's a culture within the company," he said. "This company is likely to have known about his actions before yesterday, and I think that has to be investigated as well." House bills have been filed to prevent this issue from happening again, Capriglione said. "We have legislation that will make sure that these government contracts have even more transparency and accountability, that we prevent anybody who uses these funds to go after private citizens, to go after state employees or anyone else," he said. "If any company does something like this again, they will never get a government contract again."" ($) " Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick says he'll push for special session if THC ban, bail changes fail," Texas Tribune'sJasper Scherer and Kayla Guo -- "Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick said he will move to force an overtime session of the Legislature if lawmakers fail to ban THC or tighten Texas' bail laws -- two of his top priorities -- before the current session ends in early June. The power to order lawmakers back to Austin for a special session is reserved for Gov. Greg Abbott , who also gets to set the agenda for such overtime rounds. But in his role presiding over the Texas Senate, Patrick can block any bill from passing, giving him leverage to compel special sessions by killing must-pass legislation. Patrick in 2017, of a "sunset" bill that would have extended the life of several state agencies, including the Texas Medical Board, after the House declined to take up measures curbing property tax rates and requiring transgender people to use public restrooms based on "biological sex" rather than their gender identities. In an interview, Patrick affirmed that he would go a similar route this session if the House declines to get on board with his priority bill to clamp down on the state's exploding hemp market by banning products that contain tetrahydrocannabinol, or THC. "There aren't many things you go down that path for, but the life and health of people is one," Patrick told The Texas Tribune on Wednesday. "I couldn't, in good conscience, leave here knowing if we don't do something about it in the next two years -- how many kids get sick?" Patrick and Senate lawmakers are taking aim at the roughly 8,300 Texas retailers that sell a range of hemp products -- from gummies to beverages to flower buds -- under a 2019 state law that authorized the sale of consumable hemp. Patrick and Sen. Charles Perry , the Lubbock Republican who carried the 2019 law, say the hemp industry has exploited a loophole in a bill that was intended to boost agriculture by allowing non-consumable products with small amounts of delta-9 THC. While hemp products are not allowed to contain more than a 0.3% concentration of delta-9 THC -- anything higher is classified as marijuana -- Patrick and Perry contend that the industry has endangered public health by putting products on the shelf with dangerously high levels of THC well beyond the 0.3% threshold. Perry's proposal this session, known as , would effectively shutter the hemp industry by making it illegal to possess or manufacture products containing THC outside the state's limited medical marijuana program. It's already passed in the Senate, but awaits action in the lower chamber where industry leaders are hopeful House members will push for in lieu of banning THC products altogether. Patrick said he would invoke the nuclear option of forcing a special session over anything less than an outright ban. "You just can't regulate it. You've gotta take it out," Patrick said. "You're never going to be able to regulate it." Patrick did not say which bills he might use to compel Abbott to call lawmakers back, but he has a number of hostage options. Among them is the two-year state budget, the only item the Legislature is constitutionally required to pass each session. Patrick of holding the budget hostage in 2017, though it was the sunset bill that ultimately led to a special session. A handful of key agencies are also up for sunset review this year, meaning they will cease to exist unless lawmakers pass legislation extending their life until the next periodic review. the Texas Department of Criminal Justice, the Department of Information Resources and four regional water authorities, which distribute water and operate key infrastructure around the state. Patrick also said in the interview that he'd force an overtime session if the Legislature failed to amend the state's bail laws to keep certain criminal defendants in jail as they await the resolution of their cases. "People are dying because of issues with bail," he said." STATE GOVERNMENT " Judge places injunction, shutting down Texas midwife's clinics amid illegal abortion lawsuit," San Antonio Express-News'Megan Rodriguez -- " accused of performing an illegal abortion cannot reopen while a civil lawsuit against her proceeds, a state judge ruled Thursday. Waller County District Judge Gary Chaney granted a temporary injunction Tuesday against the clinics in Cypress, Katy, Spring and Waller, all of which are affiliated with Maria Margarita Rojas. The injunction prohibits Rojas or any of her employees from providing any medical services, including abortion. Rojas, 49, is the first person in Texas to be prosecuted under Texas' strict abortion law passed in 2022. Last week, she was arrested and accused of providing an abortion to a woman out of a clinic in Waller. The hearing in Hempstead, about 50 miles northwest of downtown Houston, was also the first time Rojas and her attorneys made public statements about the case against her. Rojas was called to the stand by the AG's office to answer questions about her clinics and the alleged abortions. She invoked her Fifth Amendment rights against self-incrimination more than 200 times, and didn't answer any of the questions asked of her. The Texas Attorney General's office, which is prosecuting the case in Waller County, argued Rojas does not fall under the state's limited exceptions on who can perform an abortion, and also accused her of practicing medicine without a license. A licensed midwife, she is accused of presenting herself as a medical doctor to patients at the clinics. Chaney on Thursday said he felt Amy Hill, the chief of the AG's Healthcare Program Enforcement Division, had presented enough evidence employees at the clinics might have been operating without proper medical licenses. "I'm really worried about someone out there being a doctor that shouldn't really be a doctor," Chaney said. Chaney signed a restraining order putting similar restrictions in place last week. Thursday's hearing was held to decide if the orders would be in place for a longer period of time. Rojas was brought to the hearing wearing a pink, jail-issued jumpsuit because at the start of the day she was still being held in custody. Midway through the day, Rojas' attorneys announced she had posted her more-than $1.4 million bond. She was given a change of clothes and changed during the lunch break. Rojas' attorneys called the AG's office case "rank speculation" and "pure conjecture," and argued that a criminal complaint written by an AG's office investigator didn't prove that abortions were being done at the clinic." ($) LOCAL GOVERNMENT " Harris County commissioners keep Christian Menefee as county attorney until election is called to replace Sylvester Turner," Houston Chronicle'sAbby Church -- "Harris County Commissioners have opted to keep as the county attorney until Gov. Greg Abbott to fill the late U.S. Rep. Sylvester Turner's seat in Congress. Menefee has served as county attorney for more than four years, and recently to replace Turner, who following "enduring health complications" at 70 years old. It's the second time officials have had to race to fill the seat in the last year. In July, former U.S. Rep. Sheila Jackson Lee died after a battle with pancreatic cancer. Turner had only recently stepped in to fill her shoes in January. Under state law, Menefee's campaign filing and announcement triggered his automatic from his position as county attorney. "Resign to run" laws in Texas dictate that certain local office holders cannot announce campaigns for another seat more than a year and 30 days before the next election. If they announce any sooner, they're forced to step back from their current position. Menefee, who recently won another term as county attorney, filed for Congress hours after Turner's funeral. However, another law holds that the person is allowed to until a successor is named. Abbott's office hasn't yet called an election to replace Turner, who represented a solidly Democratic congressional district. The absence of a representative in the seat effectively leaves the Democrats shorthanded. Republicans currently hold the . Donna Davidson , a legislative and campaign lawyer based in Austin, said she has seen instances where office holders announce a campaign for another position and are replaced immediately. Others, however, have been allowed to stick around, she said. "It really just depends," Davidson said. "Let's say you've been a very effective county attorney. They don't necessarily want to make a change if they don't have to." The commissioners, who are in charge of naming Menefee's replacement until an election is called, decided on Thursday to not take action to replace him given the disruption choosing a new county attorney might cause. "Right now, I think we're in good hands," said Commissioner Adrian Garcia." ($) TEXANS IN DC " Crockett digs in amid backlash over Abbott insult," The Hill'sSaul Elbein andCheyanne M. Daniels -- "Rep. Jasmine Crockett(D-Texas) is under fire for mocking Texas Gov.Greg Abbott(R), the latest in a string of provocative statements that have boosted her profile over the past year. Since Crockett called Abbott, who is a wheelchair user, "Governor Hot Wheels," Rep. Randy Weber (R-Texas) announced , calling the remark "the latest in a series of inappropriate comments." The remarks -- which Crockett insists didn't apply to Abbott's disability -- drew condemnation from prominent Texas and national Republicans, as well as some liberal accounts online. Trump called her a "lowlife"; Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) called the remarks "shameful"; his potential future challenger, state Attorney General Ken Paxton(R), went a step further and called Crockett herself "despicable." And Abbott argued that Crockett's remarks presaged future Democratic defeats. "The bottom line is that Republican states like Texas are leading the way, and with comments like this by Democrats, we will just leave them in the dust in future elections," Abbott said to Fox News's Sean Hannity. Conservative commentators piled on as well, with the network's Lisa Kennedy Montgomery used to call Crockett an attention-seeker. Crockett doubled down despite the backlash, dismissing Republican criticism over the Abbott affair as performative outrage. She referred to Abbott's habit of busing migrants to northern cities -- particularly those with Black mayors. But on Tuesday she also declared herself "appalled that the very people who unequivocally support Trump -- a man known for racially insensitive nicknames and mocking those with disabilities -- are now outraged." In a post on the social platform X on Wednesday, she argued that Republicans had seized on her remarks to divert attention from 'Signal-gate,' a scandal in which Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth appeared to to Jeffrey Goldberg, editor of The Atlantic. "The incompetence that many of us knew existed prior to the confirmation of these individuals is on full display for the WORLD," . "But you know, keep being distracted with the faux outrage from people who have never met an empathetic bone." "Oh, and the fact that there is an obsession over wanting me silenced tells me that I need to speak out more," she added. Crockett's office did not respond to a request for comment from The Hill." “**Parole decision reached for Selena 's killer Yolanda Saldivar,**” San Antonio Express-News' **Gabriella Ybarra** and**Nancy M. Preyor-Johnson** — “**Yolanda Saldívar** , the convicted killer of Tejano music icon **Selena Quintanilla-Perez** , will remain in prison, the state’s parole board announced.

**“Health care CEO fired after Texas House DOGE hearing** ,” Dallas Morning News'**Karen Brooks Harper** and **Nolan D. McCaskill** — "The chief executive of a private health insurance company who admitted in a legislative hearing Wednesday to hiring private investigators to spy on customers has been fired.

The dismissal of Superior HealthPlan CEO **Mark Sanders** follows his testimony Wednesday to the Texas House Delivery of Government Efficiency Committee in a hearing on Medicaid procurement, during which he acknowledged hiring private investigators to get background information on lawmakers and others.

“The conduct highlighted yesterday during the course of the Texas House Committee hearing is not reflective of our values nor is it a practice Centene’s current leadership condones,” Centene, Superior’s parent company, said in a statement to _The Dallas Morning News_. “To this end, Mark Sanders is no longer with our organization.”

Sanders’ termination comes hours after Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** announced he was investigating the company over the allegations aired inside the Capitol on Wednesday.

“The allegations concerning Superior’s actions, such as actions that were characterized as potentially blackmailing lawmakers to secure state contracts and surveilling private citizens to avoid paying legitimate claims, are deeply troubling,” Paxton said in a statement. “I will get to the bottom of this, uncover any illegal activity, and hold bad actors responsible.”

At the center of the probe is a series of private investigations, starting in 2017 and allegedly ordered by Sanders, who had just taken the helm as chief executive officer of Superior. The health care firm was facing lawsuits at the time over declining coverage.

Sanders, who headed one of the state’s biggest providers of health insurance for children on Medicaid, told lawmakers under questioning Wednesday that investigators had done “routine” background checks into several state representatives, senators, health care providers, patients and their families, and a journalist several years ago.

The company has abandoned that practice, Sanders told the committee during a tense hearing he acknowledged was “rough” for him.

“We’ve done what I would call general research,” Sanders said. “Anything that’s publicly available.”

Centene said it regretted the impact Sanders’ conduct has had on the company’s partners.

“Superior’s credibility rests on being a trusted partner to our members, government stakeholders and providers,” Centene said. “While we took the necessary steps to ensure this conduct was stopped a number of years ago, yesterday’s hearing made clear we failed to address its full impact.”

“We are committed to building transparent and trusted relationships with our government partners and remain focused on our mission to improve the health and well-being of the Texas communities we serve,” the statement added.

The subjects of those investigations included Texas Land Commissioner **Dawn Buckingham** , then a state senator, and Southlake Republican state Rep. **Giovanni Capriglione** , according to documents obtained by _The Dallas Morning News_.

“You’ve hired private investigators to look at not only but also people who have filed claims and felt that they deserved those claims but that you felt that they didn’t,” Capriglione, chairman of the DOGE committee, said at Wednesday’s hearing.

“You were doing that for what purpose?” he asked. “Why would you go and run a background check, hire a private investigator to follow, to dig into the records of people who are your customers?”

In an interview Thursday, Capriglione said while it was good Sanders is no longer with the company, Paxton’s investigation should proceed.

“When this happens, it’s a culture within the company,” he said. “This company is likely to have known about his actions before yesterday, and I think that has to be investigated as well.”

House bills have been filed to prevent this issue from happening again, Capriglione said.

Preyor-Johnson — “Yolanda Saldívar , the convicted killer of Tejano music icon Selena Quintanilla-Perez , will remain in prison, the state’s parole board announced. The decision came Thursday, after the Texas Board of Pardons and Paroles voted to deny the release of Saldívar — who has been serving a life sentence at the Patrick O’Daniel Unit prison in Gatesville — for fatally shooting Selena on March 31, 1995, in Corpus Christi. Saldívar, a native of San Antonio, was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison on Oct. 26, 1995. She was required to serve 30 years before becoming eligible for parole consideration. Her parole eligibility date was set for March 30. According to a statement from the parole board, the parole review process began about six months before her parole eligibility date A parole officer prepared the case summary file to submit to the parole board voting panel. “Within that confidential file, there is a plethora of information including but not limited to court documents, offense reports, support/protest information, criminal history, institutional adjustment, and information/statements provided by the offender,” the statement continued. “The file was then sent to a parole panel of three. A simple majority was required to either grant or deny parole.” After considering all available information, including confidential interviews, the panel denied Saldívar, 64, parole. The reason cited by the panel for denial was the “nature of the offense.” “The record indicates that the instant offense has elements of brutality, violence, assaultive behavior or conscious selection of victim’s vulnerability indicating a conscious disregard for the lives, safety, or property of others, such that the offender poses a continuing threat to public safety,” the statement read. Recently, Saldívar’s family said Saldívar believes Selena was at least partly at fault because she was “forceful” in confronting Saldívar about allegedly embezzling funds. Selena, known as the “Queen of Tejano,” was 23 years old when she was killed after meeting with then 32-year-old Saldívar at the Days Inn hotel in Corpus Christi to retrieve financial records." ($) | #TXLEGE “Health care CEO fired after Texas House DOGE hearing ,” Dallas Morning News'Karen Brooks Harper and Nolan D. McCaskill — "The chief executive of a private health insurance company who admitted in a legislative hearing Wednesday to hiring private investigators to spy on customers has been fired. The dismissal of Superior HealthPlan CEO Mark Sanders follows his testimony Wednesday to the Texas House Delivery of Government Efficiency Committee in a hearing on Medicaid procurement, during which he acknowledged hiring private investigators to get background information on lawmakers and others. “The conduct highlighted yesterday during the course of the Texas House Committee hearing is not reflective of our values nor is it a practice Centene’s current leadership condones,” Centene, Superior’s parent company, said in a statement to The Dallas Morning News. “To this end, Mark Sanders is no longer with our organization.” Sanders’ termination comes hours after Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton announced he was investigating the company over the allegations aired inside the Capitol on Wednesday. “The allegations concerning Superior’s actions, such as actions that were characterized as potentially blackmailing lawmakers to secure state contracts and surveilling private citizens to avoid paying legitimate claims, are deeply troubling,” Paxton said in a statement. “I will get to the bottom of this, uncover any illegal activity, and hold bad actors responsible.” At the center of the probe is a series of private investigations, starting in 2017 and allegedly ordered by Sanders, who had just taken the helm as chief executive officer of Superior. The health care firm was facing lawsuits at the time over declining coverage. Sanders, who headed one of the state’s biggest providers of health insurance for children on Medicaid, told lawmakers under questioning Wednesday that investigators had done “routine” background checks into several state representatives, senators, health care providers, patients and their families, and a journalist several years ago. The company has abandoned that practice, Sanders told the committee during a tense hearing he acknowledged was “rough” for him. “We’ve done what I would call general research,” Sanders said. “Anything that’s publicly available.” Centene said it regretted the impact Sanders’ conduct has had on the company’s partners. “Superior’s credibility rests on being a trusted partner to our members, government stakeholders and providers,” Centene said. “While we took the necessary steps to ensure this conduct was stopped a number of years ago, yesterday’s hearing made clear we failed to address its full impact.” “We are committed to building transparent and trusted relationships with our government partners and remain focused on our mission to improve the health and well-being of the Texas communities we serve,” the statement added. The subjects of those investigations included Texas Land Commissioner Dawn Buckingham , then a state senator, and Southlake Republican state Rep. Giovanni Capriglione , according to documents obtained by The Dallas Morning News. “You’ve hired private investigators to look at not only but also people who have filed claims and felt that they deserved those claims but that you felt that they didn’t,” Capriglione, chairman of the DOGE committee, said at Wednesday’s hearing. “You were doing that for what purpose?” he asked. “Why would you go and run a background check, hire a private investigator to follow, to dig into the records of people who are your customers?” In an interview Thursday, Capriglione said while it was good Sanders is no longer with the company, Paxton’s investigation should proceed. “When this happens, it’s a culture within the company,” he said. “This company is likely to have known about his actions before yesterday, and I think that has to be investigated as well.” House bills have been filed to prevent this issue from happening again, Capriglione said. “We have legislation that will make sure that these government contracts have even more transparency and accountability, that we prevent anybody who uses these funds to go after private citizens, to go after state employees or anyone else,” he said. “If any company does something like this again, they will never get a government contract again.”" ($) “Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick says he’ll push for special session if THC ban, bail changes fail ,” Texas Tribune'sJasper Scherer and Kayla Guo — "Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick said he will move to force an overtime session of the Legislature if lawmakers fail to ban THC or tighten Texas’ bail laws — two of his top priorities — before the current session ends in early June. The power to order lawmakers back to Austin for a special session is reserved for Gov. Greg Abbott , who also gets to set the agenda for such overtime rounds. But in his role presiding over the Texas Senate, Patrick can block any bill from passing, giving him leverage to compel special sessions by killing must-pass legislation. Patrick in 2017, of a “sunset” bill that would have extended the life of several state agencies, including the Texas Medical Board, after the House declined to take up measures curbing property tax rates and requiring transgender people to use public restrooms based on “biological sex” rather than their gender identities. In an interview, Patrick affirmed that he would go a similar route this session if the House declines to get on board with his priority bill to clamp down on the state’s exploding hemp market by banning products that contain tetrahydrocannabinol, or THC. “There aren’t many things you go down that path for, but the life and health of people is one,” Patrick told The Texas Tribune on Wednesday. “I couldn’t, in good conscience, leave here knowing if we don't do something about it in the next two years — how many kids get sick?” Patrick and Senate lawmakers are taking aim at the roughly 8,300 Texas retailers that sell a range of hemp products — from gummies to beverages to flower buds — under a 2019 state law that authorized the sale of consumable hemp. Patrick and Sen. Charles Perry , the Lubbock Republican who carried the 2019 law, say the hemp industry has exploited a loophole in a bill that was intended to boost agriculture by allowing non-consumable products with small amounts of delta-9 THC. While hemp products are not allowed to contain more than a 0.3% concentration of delta-9 THC — anything higher is classified as marijuana — Patrick and Perry contend that the industry has endangered public health by putting products on the shelf with dangerously high levels of THC well beyond the 0.3% threshold. Perry’s proposal this session, known as , would effectively shutter the hemp industry by making it illegal to possess or manufacture products containing THC outside the state’s limited medical marijuana program. It’s already passed in the Senate, but awaits action in the lower chamber where industry leaders are hopeful House members will push for in lieu of banning THC products altogether. Patrick said he would invoke the nuclear option of forcing a special session over anything less than an outright ban. “You just can’t regulate it. You’ve gotta take it out,” Patrick said. “You’re never going to be able to regulate it.” Patrick did not say which bills he might use to compel Abbott to call lawmakers back, but he has a number of hostage options. Among them is the two-year state budget, the only item the Legislature is constitutionally required to pass each session. Patrick of holding the budget hostage in 2017, though it was the sunset bill that ultimately led to a special session. A handful of key agencies are also up for sunset review this year, meaning they will cease to exist unless lawmakers pass legislation extending their life until the next periodic review. the Texas Department of Criminal Justice, the Department of Information Resources and four regional water authorities, which distribute water and operate key infrastructure around the state. Patrick also said in the interview that he’d force an overtime session if the Legislature failed to amend the state’s bail laws to keep certain criminal defendants in jail as they await the resolution of their cases. “People are dying because of issues with bail,” he said." | STATE GOVERNMENT “Judge places injunction, shutting down Texas midwife 's clinics amid illegal abortion lawsuit," San Antonio Express-News'Megan Rodriguez — " accused of performing an illegal abortion cannot reopen while a civil lawsuit against her proceeds, a state judge ruled Thursday. Waller County District Judge Gary Chaney granted a temporary injunction Tuesday against the clinics in Cypress, Katy, Spring and Waller, all of which are affiliated with Maria Margarita Rojas. The injunction prohibits Rojas or any of her employees from providing any medical services, including abortion. Rojas, 49, is the first person in Texas to be prosecuted under Texas’ strict abortion law passed in 2022. Last week, she was arrested and accused of providing an abortion to a woman out of a clinic in Waller. The hearing in Hempstead, about 50 miles northwest of downtown Houston, was also the first time Rojas and her attorneys made public statements about the case against her. Rojas was called to the stand by the AG’s office to answer questions about her clinics and the alleged abortions. She invoked her Fifth Amendment rights against self-incrimination more than 200 times, and didn’t answer any of the questions asked of her. The Texas Attorney General’s office, which is prosecuting the case in Waller County, argued Rojas does not fall under the state’s limited exceptions on who can perform an abortion, and also accused her of practicing medicine without a license. A licensed midwife, she is accused of presenting herself as a medical doctor to patients at the clinics. Chaney on Thursday said he felt Amy Hill, the chief of the AG’s Healthcare Program Enforcement Division, had presented enough evidence employees at the clinics might have been operating without proper medical licenses. “I’m really worried about someone out there being a doctor that shouldn’t really be a doctor,” Chaney said. Chaney signed a restraining order putting similar restrictions in place last week. Thursday's hearing was held to decide if the orders would be in place for a longer period of time. Rojas was brought to the hearing wearing a pink, jail-issued jumpsuit because at the start of the day she was still being held in custody. Midway through the day, Rojas’ attorneys announced she had posted her more-than $1.4 million bond. She was given a change of clothes and changed during the lunch break. Rojas’ attorneys called the AG’s office case “rank speculation” and “pure conjecture,” and argued that a criminal complaint written by an AG’s office investigator didn’t prove that abortions were being done at the clinic." ($) | LOCAL GOVERNMENT “Harris County commissioners keep Christian Menefee as county attorney until election is called to replace Sylvester Turner ,” Houston Chronicle'sAbby Church — "Harris County Commissioners have opted to keep as the county attorney until Gov. Greg Abbott to fill the late U.S. Rep. Sylvester Turner 's seat in Congress. Menefee has served as county attorney for more than four years, and recently to replace Turner, who following “enduring health complications” at 70 years old. It’s the second time officials have had to race to fill the seat in the last year. In July, former U.S. Rep. Sheila Jackson Lee died after a battle with pancreatic cancer. Turner had only recently stepped in to fill her shoes in January. Under state law, Menefee’s campaign filing and announcement triggered his automatic from his position as county attorney. “Resign to run” laws in Texas dictate that certain local office holders cannot announce campaigns for another seat more than a year and 30 days before the next election. If they announce any sooner, they’re forced to step back from their current position. Menefee, who recently won another term as county attorney, filed for Congress hours after Turner’s funeral. However, another law holds that the person is allowed to until a successor is named. Abbott’s office hasn't yet called an election to replace Turner, who represented a solidly Democratic congressional district. The absence of a representative in the seat effectively leaves the Democrats shorthanded. Republicans currently hold the . Donna Davidson , a legislative and campaign lawyer based in Austin, said she has seen instances where office holders announce a campaign for another position and are replaced immediately. Others, however, have been allowed to stick around, she said. “It really just depends,” Davidson said. “Let's say you've been a very effective county attorney. They don't necessarily want to make a change if they don't have to.” The commissioners, who are in charge of naming Menefee’s replacement until an election is called, decided on Thursday to not take action to replace him given the disruption choosing a new county attorney might cause. “Right now, I think we’re in good hands,” said Commissioner Adrian Garcia." ($) | TEXANS IN DC “Crockett digs in amid backlash over Abbott insult ,” The Hill'sSaul Elbein andCheyanne M. Daniels — "Rep. Jasmine Crockett(D-Texas) is under fire for mocking Texas Gov.Greg Abbott(R), the latest in a string of provocative statements that have boosted her profile over the past year. Since Crockett called Abbott, who is a wheelchair user, “Governor Hot Wheels,” Rep. Randy Weber (R-Texas) announced , calling the remark “the latest in a series of inappropriate comments.” The remarks — which Crockett insists didn’t apply to Abbott’s disability — drew condemnation from prominent Texas and national Republicans, as well as some liberal accounts online. Trump called her a “lowlife”; Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) called the remarks “shameful”; his potential future challenger, state Attorney General Ken Paxton(R), went a step further and called Crockett herself “despicable.” And Abbott argued that Crockett’s remarks presaged future Democratic defeats. “The bottom line is that Republican states like Texas are leading the way, and with comments like this by Democrats, we will just leave them in the dust in future elections,” Abbott said to Fox News’s Sean Hannity. Conservative commentators piled on as well, with the network’s Lisa Kennedy Montgomery used to call Crockett an attention-seeker. Crockett doubled down despite the backlash, dismissing Republican criticism over the Abbott affair as performative outrage. name: Hillsdale College via 1600 Daily
subject: Helpful video on the Electoral College
body:
Most Americans need to understand how the Electoral College works and its role in preserving free and representative government.

This sponsored message from 1600 Daily is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | | [](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zk7o9p6j66bcjcedfl7ehudege1utqp3ekttajuo_rp22sh2s8i6eob6chim6o37clh2bs)
---
| | Dear Fellow American,

I want to share with you a free video that explains the Electoral College as devised by the Framers of our Constitution and how it works today.

[**It 's called "The Electoral College Explained."**](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2z2e36ga67ceibu5fagqv71uricu5ukrm7j1o97r8_rp22sh2s8i6eob6chim6o37clh2bs)

[](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2z4i7c958ac4s0ipqci9paao6g8poc63gljnnpsc0_rp22sh2s8i6eob6chim6o37clh2bs)
Most Americans need to understand how the Electoral College works and its role in preserving free and representative government.

But after you watch this video, you'll learn...
* Why the American Founders created the Electoral College and how the two-party system changes the way it functions

* How the Electoral College prevents political campaigns from focusing only on urban--and not rural--voters; and

* What presidential elections would look like without the Electoral College and how the national popular vote could lead to a _decrease_ in election integrity.

As you can see, this free twelve-minute video taught by Hillsdale College politics professor Kevin Portteus is packed with critical information so many Americans don't know--even patriotic Americans who love this country.

They may understand that the Electoral College is important but can't explain why.

**It 's not their fault. **

Too many schools nationwide have abandoned teaching about these important constitutional principles in favor of critical race theory, transgender ideology, or whatever Marxist ideology they dress up in some new "woke" lingo.

**But it 's _never_ too late to learn. **

After watching "The Electoral College Explained," one viewer commented on YouTube, _" This makes so much more sense now. Thanks!"_

**Here 's a link to watch the video.**

[**https://info.hillsdale.edu/electoral-college-video**](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2z9f90o9risg8ue17e0ggmln68pedp3mqubjru9mg_rp22sh2s8i6eob6chim6o37clh2bs)

When you watch, you're guaranteed to understand everything we stand to lose if we replace the Electoral College with a national popular vote.

And when the far-Left works to keep Americans ignorant of our institutions--and why they are important--your willingness to learn is one ESSENTIAL way you'll fight for our country on the battlefield of education.

Thank you.

Warm regards,

Labin Duke, Th.M.
Associate Vice President
National Donor Outreach
Hillsdale College

name: Hillsdale College via First Look News
subject: Helpful video on the Electoral College
body:
Most Americans need to understand how the Electoral College works and its role in preserving free and representative government.

This sponsored message from First Look is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | | [](https://e.firstlook.news/rd/9z2zaaps38291nfku6g5s9qsa16jia1sn8vbcb5qui8_rp22sh2s8i6eob6chim9or6cph2bs)
---
| | Dear Fellow American,

I want to share with you a free video that explains the Electoral College as devised by the Framers of our Constitution and how it works today.

[**It 's called "The Electoral College Explained."**](https://e.firstlook.news/rd/9z2z5srjn14nl98q2rfhnrg1b2iv14pn4c83eqmdu50_rp22sh2s8i6eob6chim9or6cph2bs)

[](https://e.firstlook.news/rd/9z2zb5q8fej692gjccujqp5j3g218mfhm48muqivqdo_rp22sh2s8i6eob6chim9or6cph2bs)
Most Americans need to understand how the Electoral College works and its role in preserving free and representative government.

But after you watch this video, you'll learn...
* Why the American Founders created the Electoral College and how the two-party system changes the way it functions

* How the Electoral College prevents political campaigns from focusing only on urban--and not rural--voters; and

* What presidential elections would look like without the Electoral College and how the national popular vote could lead to a _decrease_ in election integrity.

As you can see, this free twelve-minute video taught by Hillsdale College politics professor Kevin Portteus is packed with critical information so many Americans don't know--even patriotic Americans who love this country.

They may understand that the Electoral College is important but can't explain why.

**It 's not their fault. **

Too many schools nationwide have abandoned teaching about these important constitutional principles in favor of critical race theory, transgender ideology, or whatever Marxist ideology they dress up in some new "woke" lingo.

**But it 's _never_ too late to learn. **

After watching "The Electoral College Explained," one viewer commented on YouTube, _" This makes so much more sense now. Thanks!"_

**Here 's a link to watch the video.**

[**https://info.hillsdale.edu/electoral-college-video**](https://e.firstlook.news/rd/9z2zn3qvjg2tb5a0j2ucjpe8uh4d7v2aslb9mtartgg_rp22sh2s8i6eob6chim9or6cph2bs)

When you watch, you're guaranteed to understand everything we stand to lose if we replace the Electoral College with a national popular vote.

And when the far-Left works to keep Americans ignorant of our institutions--and why they are important--your willingness to learn is one ESSENTIAL way you'll fight for our country on the battlefield of education.

Thank you.

Warm regards,

Labin Duke, Th.M.
Associate Vice President
National Donor Outreach
Hillsdale College

## RFK Jr. to Cut 10,000 Federal Health Jobs
Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. announced plans to [eliminate 10,000 federal health jobs](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0zzFvwyAUBOBfgzesx8MYMjB08ZauHS0Cj0CKTWTTWPn3lbt3O-mk73Rf1_nqcsnr_dMtZFusMwIqDpKjmYPL5T0PXbCRCEl2ZIUepFCjxLFL1qMUjlQwIgaJ5C8AoOKowOgYNYku21MDiUYAKIReRxPiSIgqmsvNDGwACrnVrX_UvLZEsbzri7be16UrNrX23Jn8YDgxnI7j6P1682fJcDpphhPIM2uG0xa_-WPjz-LWnQsAAJ7Szh_1xv1P2_vUltJtNjyPXEreR80GuC8ul7-19t_7l8XfAAAA__-AtFkF), shrinking the department’s workforce by nearly 25%. The cuts, part of a broader reorganization, will impact agencies including the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the Food and Drug Administration, and the National Institutes of Health. The department also plans to close half its regional offices. [**https://info.hillsdale.edu/electoral-college-video**](https://links.defend-the-constitution.org/s/c/e5W5MNEdHfuiPmsp97zXHeUADUoK0BTOcZT-LKK8zJJxdHPn_QK2HgAbScXS7Os01XKmBPcNpHAS976zt7WFWSCs8CViXLOiWts05KQOAbsci311dC899y1aPHwy6eNVwa07lbePmpP6dEXZGLF9wCVTgTArp42Qjb7E2KLfbKh-lB8oE0pAgp4qcEwkl9chU3R4c5m5NUZUKj6GoboQneeyuvtoanLtHEjRvtcKqVP0KD7OIPbR25TjOL4RN6GKeAEputB4W7cL2pMnumksmLOBE9SxcsUD0l0zAmqvbl06bu2wfDo5Nah0iFdKhtongjIidfUxkn-vfZ80eyWDcabqld4d2YPWxV_KDiwjClpjiSjhso-EXGXdOWNY5gtMuFat_eVPktZq7DCFlRR9EK69aeEYu7p6fn7DqOS0uES5BhCDmO4MtAFthLc80PJ21iJRcgQFresxfm-Vy_ibMjw/NYE5PltRxeuY82zNf_aKCep1N32VZlaY/7)

When you watch, you'll better understand everything we stand to lose if we replace the Electoral College with a national popular vote.

Thanks for your help.

# **Trump’s Deportations Without Due Process**
---
| [](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2wxt0h-vxo5vi-kyd76rh7/)
---

## Judge: Prisons Without A/C 'Unconstitutional'
In a Wednesday ruling, a federal judge said housing inmates in Texas prisons without air conditioning during periods of extreme heat is “plainly unconstitutional.” The ruling [stopped short of ordering the state to remedy the situation](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kL2OwyAQhJ8Gd1iwgH8Kimvc5dorLTDreE8YIkPi5O1PSX_tjL7R6Pu5zBdHkdL12-1o63PNMwgwXCgOwxwcxdesm2C9CKNs0MpeK2nGTo3NZkEqMwzSI4R-wKWDbjHarEaoXkvvdEP2PSYUDFKYQep2xb4bfO9x9M4ZpZgWGKjmo60bVny6ssZXfuDRLnlvot1qvRWmvhhMDKbzPNvFl4RnefcMpg_CYHpHDKYVAx4u8t97uCIv7lU4PuuBO_INXeWU-Ifgt4NKToVT4fe05FQq1XulnFxkMDWHDbeTYqTS9UyL6-4ofh7VfxU9LPwFAAD__y4da5I) in the two-thirds of prisons that aren’t fully climate-controlled. The class-action lawsuit was filed in 2023 by Bernie Tiede, a convicted murderer sentenced to life and the subject of the 2011 film _Bernie_. U.S. District Judge Robert Pittman [said that](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLuOwyAURL8GOizexgXFNumy7ZYWzr0kbIiJDAnJ36-cfsuRZs5I5-c4H0PKaT1_hxv69oplllwaxhWTboaQ8nvWFPzCYRIUvRi1EmayaqIXj1Hq6BB0HKUKRimrIIKzUVjuzEnR5HcYV9IJbpzQQ8TRumVccFrCPiCaI6RWtqFdsOEr1Jjf5YnbcCo3mv2ltXsl6ovIA5GH3vuwYq8d8boXiDz8PuCMbMPlccXKAAPkNzuVFVJLZa3sw2T3LdU9SW6EEpxuHu495ZyqHYnm51tI-fPY_lXw9PIvAAD__61lX5o) “excessive heat is likely serving as a form of unconstitutional punishment.” The case will now proceed to trial, where Pittman noted that prisoners and advocates are likely to prevail. Officials estimate it would [cost $1.1 billion to install air conditioning](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kD-PozAUxD8NdEb-R4DCxTV0ufZK9LAf8G4dO2ubQL79KtFKW205M_qNRvPvOl2BPIX1L9zQlHOJk-SyZVwx2U8OyD8nXTszczeIGo3otBLtcFFDvZneSiuQ8xZaBbiIQVnBldbtMjirAWoyrzKuZC942wvdLNhd-rmbcZgBWqUqzdFRiakpGxY8IS_-GR-YGhtvtTdbKfdcqT-VHCs5HsfRfJzn4xVWcgx45EqOb4x9iwUdJvDs_-5WZGn3mNk9UY6BbQiF2RgcFYohM0jI9mBjyIXK_vLAs3kvzEXMobCEnzslZEDpB6Ow1sm4-0HeU750lebrDci_95ZfD3wY-RUAAP__7pF4nQ) in all of the 100 or so state prisons and another $20 million annually to operate the systems. State law requires county jails to be kept at a temperature between 65 and 85 degrees Fahrenheit. Several bills have been filed this legislative session to require state prisons to be equipped with air conditioning.
## 'One Tough Grandma' Remembered
Carole Keeton, the first woman to serve as Texas Comptroller and the mayor of Austin, [died Wednesday at the age of 85](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kL2OwyAQBp8Gd0R4MQEKimvocu2VFjbrGB0Oltn8vf2J9NettKPR6Pu5jJeQcrpdv8OGjl5LGUGA4kJyMGMMKb_HoYtuEtH2HbpeD7JX9ixttzpEsDqqRSw6am2EtqBNMNH2Ki4wqy65JhMSTC-U6YfTgvpsJj2hnUJQUrJBYExUjhOtSPgKdcnv8sDjNJety24l2iuTXww8A193nOm4b7nMId_wWRvFwNOrPcudVv5xcMx8D7Uw8I1i4FsGAy9kuzUDP4ejZOS_iFRuPCasPBA3qjtc3J8p51TPmg3iuoWUPzH07zoPB38BAAD__2acZlk). Keeton was born in Austin and studied government at the University of Texas. She served on the board of trustees for Austin ISD before being [elected mayor of her hometown](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLvOozAUhJ_GdAdhGwcoXLAF1WaLbVIiYx-Dtb4g44Tk7Vek_6sZaaSZ0fe4z3flvIvrHxVQlrdNM2uYgIYD62ejnP_MbWXk0piBVihp13Iqhhsfqk1qO_SU0sVYqnFALSjlhmltF0aZsF3l5FXWcNbTRvS0rS12t37pFhwWpQTnpG3QuJJyXTYs-FaH9Z_0wlzrFCovt1L2g_CRsImw6TzPOhzxygibMMLzIGyKeF6yJ--K05dNEaGk57rBmlU0QYFNOWCG7wLoFPaSk_eYQaucPMI_xJIiGFQGVIFeEDapDONIf_1-jH-rLM1-Ou_dcetI26xBOf-9WH5k9pLsfwAAAP__HT5wjQ) in 1977, serving three terms. Keeton was also elected to the Texas Railroad Commission, where she served from 1994 to 1999. In 2006, she ran as an independent candidate for governor, referring to herself as “one tough grandma” and [garnering 18% of the vote](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0z0FqAyEUgOHT6C6DPh11Fi5KIbt0VehSnvE5EUwcHJsmty_pvgf4P_i_TuGEpZbb-oFX8uORWwAB80GoA7iQsNRn0Dz5KNIiOXlptZLzYtTCL95lDXqWC52jRpOiBqMykrNZ2CQIePEvTChwUsxO6imTNS7aSEtEnJViWlAqo_VpXGjQA_dcn-1OfTq3K6_-Msa2M_XG4MjgGLHWNjZKBafWVwbHz1cS1u9I_Yaj9YI1UKXzKO3G4D2AEIZ3n7afUmvZjWVarFcs9c8f_w7fPfwGAAD__w9SWUk) to finish third. In an [obituary](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx00L2OqzAQQOGnsTuQmeHHLlzchi633RLZ8ZCM1uAIJiG8_Srbb3_0FefrMl0CZ15v_8NCXt5zmcBAVxmswE4pcD6nVicfTXKNJt8MLTad69HpuydEtIN1yczuavuYbEyIEJF6SrZ3mv0HMwi2MZ1t2nqmobdxiORiCB2iag0llrLVciehd9jnfJYXbfW1LDr7u8hjV_hPwahgPI6jTnxbWc6FlrJxyJ9OwVgiyzNsTLuCMTx34bWSt4LxGraSqfomkrJWDaCxzqHefHocnDPv_aBac1sC_1Ja_nzw8vATAAD__-3LX1s), Keeton’s family praised her as “a trailblazer for women, embodying the best of public service and inspiring younger generations to serve.” Yesterday, Gov. Greg Abbott ordered flags to [fly at half-staff](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kEGL4yAcxT-NuTXoX6PJwUPZTZaF7Q50CnMUjZoIpgbjZNpvP6T3Of0uj8fvvY-LuugQw336rxcny8MnBRiaE6YnaJXVIT4Vq6w02HakcpIIRknTcdpVswTPMYzUj9xQIpihhmHeirZriAE-QhXkUYYptAQ3LWG1d4K3RhjXGa0bShHDzoaScl1mV9xDbz4-0-5yPaalinIuZd0QPSMYEAxT2utXqJ7SjmD4XGPSdkMw-BDdwTW77eC__nbrr-rt-ru_Kp_y4rL6lZa15BSjy-q9ZP2cU76rv5fzn14dc8XpkK1X66ss7foVYgwbF4jhadEhvozKjxftEr4DAAD__z0saJQ) in her honor until sunset today.
## Waldorf Astoria Coming to Fredericksburg
The state’s first-ever Waldorf Astoria Hotel and Resort is [coming to Fredericksburg](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kL2O8yAQAJ8Gd7Zg8Q8uKL7GXb72SmuBJUaHTQQ4id_-lOuvH81I83VbbxhiOO7_cSdd3z6twGFouWxBrQ5DvNa-cdpwN4uGtJh6KYZ5lHOzaTVaGAgVeDtILvnIR7RCKCOlMpzPTdAfGZegBB-U6DtP06jMZGg2iIOUrOfkQk25qxtVemPx8UpPyp1NexP1VuujMPmPwcJgwbPUcHT2jPXMtOPjQzFYDnoVBkvN-KTIYHlhdCn7FktNOWC7hRhbm86j5qv1mRzlYL-LOfOdwdJk7R6vEGMo48R6ft8xxN9-_XPIU8NPAAAA___DnmTx) in 2027. Developed through a partnership between Hilton and Wine Country Hospitality Partners, the [106-acre luxury resort](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx00LuOgzAQheGnMZ2Rb9hQuNiGLttuiQY8hJEmOAIvhLdfJf32R5-O_p_bcANiWu_f8MBYXnMejDKNVFaadkhAfA2uSnFUqdMVRh2c1U3nbVct0TrEYCcPEDw475rR6clMvrPJWD2HiuIbU9a0WjWtdvWMwbdjGLEbARprhVOYqOStLgsWfME-85UP3OopPyqOSynPXdgvYXph-vM86yUX5EQHvhfC9CueuzD9QlzyKhMeyPlJ612ewClvs4S95I1AfnS5ELOc8u9atkuYPjjru0aYvtpiep7ETLsPwqn7A4g_J8q_VY5o_gIAAP__5WNlzg) will include 60 hotel rooms, 37 resort villas, and 50 private residences. Guests and residents will also have access to an 11,000-square-foot spa and fitness center and two pools. "_Waldorf Astoria Texas Hill Country marks a significant shift for hospitality in Texas, bringing the renowned service and luxury experience of the brand to a destination with unmatched potential_ ," [said developer Robert Radovan](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0z7GO8yAQBOCnwZ2tZcEYCoq_cZe_vdJawjpGIsHCKE7e_pT0V8_oG83PZblQyulx-0939u21lgUBxx5Uj3aJlPJ70V30AaKTHXs5aSVHZ5TrNj9OozZhkpGNdYYwGLIGgB1oG4KKXfIfDBRaCaOVelh5MjZMgV0gGpUSGjimVurQNm78omPN7_LkOlzLvct-a20_hPoncBY4n-c5XLdaHp9U4Pzg8xA4U23pmvlToBxLXXs6WqmJ-q_YI6BGC3LYt72rPu5nyjkdZhIabndK-TvW_nz_9PgbAAD__-gVXA4) in a press release. Hilton Vice President Amy King called the hotel a [“monumental milestone” for the company](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx00L2O6yAQxfGnwR0RDP6ioLiNu9x2S2scxvZIBCIgcfz2q6Tf_uh3pP_Pdb4iB47bf7yTq-81zaCgk8pIGGePHM65bbxblLe6IaeH1ujO9sY2u6Obwt5b8F4DDarTypBHO-rBdla1vmH3wZSBUatu1O1lpaEfl2EhuyB2xohWkeea8qXuVOmNZQ1nelG-3NK9CW6v9VGE-SdgEjDVnR6JYy3b8_wMBEyRjiJgOjD4lFeJpabMKL-U3DkEeUvPWPMpD44kM22cooCpyc4_Dg6BSz-IVm135PA9rX9WeDn4DQAA___UyWFI), recalling that founder Conrad Hilton established Hilton in Texas over 105 years ago.

Several bills have been filed this legislative session to require state prisons to be equipped with air conditioning. 'One Tough Grandma' Remembered Carole Keeton, the first woman to serve as Texas Comptroller and the mayor of Austin, . Keeton was born in Austin and studied government at the University of Texas. She served on the board of trustees for Austin ISD before being in 1977, serving three terms. Keeton was also elected to the Texas Railroad Commission, where she served from 1994 to 1999. In 2006, she ran as an independent candidate for governor, referring to herself as “one tough grandma” and to finish third. In an , Keeton’s family praised her as “a trailblazer for women, embodying the best of public service and inspiring younger generations to serve.” Yesterday, Gov. He was born to a ruling Mongol family and was given the name [Temüjin](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sttyxg&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com), which means “of iron” or “blacksmith” in the Mongolian language. Temüjin was sent into exile with his mother and siblings when he was 9 years old, after his father was poisoned by political enemies. Despite living in poverty and even a brief enslavement, he clawed his way back to power by killing leaders of rival tribes and gathering allies. By his early 20s, he had emerged as a tribal leader with a large, loyal army.
---
In 1206, when Temüjin was in his late 30s to mid-40s (his birth year is the subject of debate), he gathered leaders — the ones he hadn’t killed — from all over the Mongolian Steppe to unite them as one nation, ready to conquer neighboring lands. At this assembly, called a _kurultai,_ he was given the title of Genghis Khan. “[Khan](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sttyxg&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)” is a Mongolian word for “leader” or “ruler,” although its use spread more widely in the following centuries. “Genghis,” also spelled “Chinggis,” is usually translated as “universal,” although it [could have](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sttyxg&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) also meant “ocean” or “just.”
While he had risen to power as Temüjin, the leader built his empire as Genghis Khan. By his death in 1227, the Mongol Empire reached north to Siberia, south to Tibet, west to the Caspian Sea, and east to the China Sea. His children and grandchildren, including the famed ruler Kublai Khan, went on to grow the territory to around 9 million square miles, making it what is still the [largest contiguous land empire in history](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sttyxg&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com). Genghis Khan’s immediate successor, Ögödei, used the title _khagan,_ meaning “Great Khan.”
[](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sttyxg&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) | [](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sttyxg&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)

## The Mongol Empire had its sights on Western Europe.
The Mongol Empire was vast, and included significant parts of Eastern Europe. The Golden Horde — the western portion of the empire, led by Genghis Khan’s grandson Batu — [conquered Kyiv](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sttyxg&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) in 1240. They laid waste to Hungary and mounted the head of Henry II, Duke of Silesia (now Poland), on a pike. Some Silesians were so terrified of the approaching army that they torched their own city and hid. Batu’s cavalry pushed its way into Bohemia in the spring of 1242, but abruptly turned back and pulled out of Hungary altogether instead of pushing further into Western Europe. There’s some debate as to why, but there are a couple of compelling theories. First, Ögödei, the Great Khan, had died in December 1241, and word may have just reached Batu that he needed to go back and help pick a successor at the _kurultai_. Second, the climate in the region had recently taken a really, really bad turn: The temperature was cold, the path was marshy, and food was scarce for both humans and horses, so the Mongols may have realized that moving forward wasn’t feasible.

Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene **[exploded at a British reporter](https://substack.com/redirect/3201d47e-7186-4cc9-a492-3887e9466d8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as she started to ask a pointed question during a press gaggle, telling her to go back to her own country that has been overrun with migrants.
[Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/3201d47e-7186-4cc9-a492-3887e9466d8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

body:
[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/62?t=1001&akid=8396%2E5257348%2E0AOKPK ]Adam Schiff for Senate

Elon Musk accused me of treason,
Derek.

The more I hold him accountable for his flagrant conflicts of interest,
the more he lashes out. It won’t stop me.

Elon took to social media to share right-wing lies about my leadership of
Trump’s first impeachment over Trump’s effort to shakedown President
Zelenskyy of Ukraine. Yes, Zelenskyy — who Trump and JD Vance viciously
took attacked in the Oval Office earlier this month.

The more things change, the more they stay the same.

But it’s not my leadership of Trump’s impeachment that has Elon seething.
It’s my exposure of his massive conflicts of interest, and his potential
violations of the law against self-dealing.

You see, I demanded information from the head of the Office of Government
Ethics as to whether Elon was violating 18 U.S.C. Section 208, which makes
it a crime to participate in government decisions affecting your own
business interests, something Elon seems to be doing every day.

But before I could get an answer, the head of that office was fired by
Trump. Along with the firing of Inspectors General, this action was
designed to facilitate the grift that is going on in the Trump
Administration.

Nevertheless, I couldn’t help but be struck by the irony: accused of
treason while Donald Trump withdrew all military aid for our ally,
Ukraine, to bow down to Vladimir Putin and Russia. I told Elon that if he
was looking for someone betraying our country and its national security
interests, he needn’t look very far.

Now, these attacks aren’t new. I’ve had a target on my back for
years, Derek.

What is new is the authority that Elon Musk, Donald Trump, and countless
right-wing officials have to weaponize the government against me and
others.

Trump has given Musk unfettered access to millions of Americans’ data.
Kash Patel is in charge of the FBI and can investigate whomever he wants.
Pam Bondi can order the Justice Department to seek vengeance against any
and all of Trump’s rivals – including me. We have already seen the Justice
Department threaten democratic officials for speaking out.

And we need to fight back.

We cannot let Elon’s lies go unanswered. And we certainly cannot turn our
backs on Ukraine and our fellow democracies around the world.

impact of our message. Ahead of my campaign’s end-of-quarter fundraising
deadline, please chip in to help our team amplify our response to Elon’s
lies.

subject: I didn’t make it this far to give up now
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
The last three months have been a gut check for a lot of us. Trump and his administration are coming for everything we hold dear. Hundreds of thousands are suffering already, and that number could go up to millions if Trump and Elon get their way.
#

It hasn’t been easy, Peter.
Growing up poor, seeing my mom struggle.
Working to help the family get by when I was just a kid.
Making my way from the south side of Chicago to Harvard.
Getting through Recruit Training in the Marines, deploying to Iraq, seeing some of the worst combat of the war.
And winning one of the closest Senate campaigns in the country last year — that wasn’t easy either.
The last three months have been a gut check for a lot of us. Trump and his administration are coming for everything we hold dear. Hundreds of thousands are suffering already, and that number could go up to millions if Trump and Elon get their way. What are we going to do about it?
I’ve got to tell you: I did not make it through all of that just to give up now.
I did not swear an oath to support and defend the Constitution to let Trump tear it to shreds. I did not lose some of my best friends in combat to cede everything I fought for to Elon Musk and a bunch of billionaires. And I sure as hell won’t sit by and watch as they bring our country to its knees.
[**For these next four years, I’m going to fight. body:
This race is more than just Virginia's future – It's going to be a bellwether for the entire nation and the first major election after Trump’s inauguration

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/104669375/536122123/1993432096?refcode=BLU_EM_ASFG_2025-03-28_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDM4NTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTJkMGExM2EtZTEwYi1mMDExLTkwY2QtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZmI3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=JCF1yarBeymFhWqfOJYbC43A1ErBCCuyhvRkGosg7oc=)

| Peter,

We’re just three days away from our March fundraising deadline, and**I wanted to share three important things you should know about Abigail’s race for Virginia Governor this November:**
1. **This race is more than just Virginia's future** – It's going to be a bellwether for the entire nation and the first major election after Trump’s inauguration. The outcome will set the stage for Democrats in 2026. So we’ve got to win big.

2. **_The Cook Political Report_ has called this race a complete TOSS-UP** – That means this race will be tough, and polls are going to stay tight right up until Election Day on November 4, 2025.

Friends --
Here is the truth, directly and transparently:
We have received a lot less individual donations this month than we had planned for, and certainly less than the last few months.
Some of the reasons are very understandable: the economy looks shaky, Elon is firing whoever he can, and there are a lot of organizations that need help during this chaotic time.
But for those who care about the issue of gun safety in America, the next few days are important for our movement—and we're hoping for lots of individual donations to sustain our work.
Every donation we receive we will be used to try to stop Trump, Elon, and Kash Patel from eroding our gun safety laws and institutions. And we'll put your donations to work electing a Congress who will stand up to their efforts.
Gabby Giffords is amazing, but she can’t do this alone. It's going to take all of us doing something that hasn't happened enough this month...Chipping in.

| | Hi Friend,
---
For nearly 70 days, Trump and his team’s extreme and aggressive actions have been a non-stop drumbeat of chaos. In so many ways, trying to overwhelm us is their goal. So I won’t sugarcoat it, reclaiming our government from Trump and his band of billionaires won’t be easy.
---
Every step of the way, I have engaged with local, grassroots leaders in Rhode Island and across our country who are standing up for our communities and against the gutting of Social Security and Medicaid, firing essential public servants, and reducing nutrition assistance. While this will be amongst the hardest missions that we’ve ever had, we do this work to be there for our people on the tough days. I’m ready to be part of the next generation of leaders to bring our country through this challenge.
---
---
_Congressman Amo speaks with local leaders at the Bristol Democratic Town Committee_
---
But our ranks are growing. Nearly every day, I get phone calls from people who are ready to do more — even running for Congress to help us flip the House of Representatives.
---
We’re just a few days away from the end of this first reporting period since Trump’s election. With your contribution, let’s send a message of encouragement that our energy to stop the chaos is strong, unified, and activated everywhere.
---

body:
We need to keep our state out of the hands of right-wing oligarchs.
| Hi Peter, it’s Ben Wikler, Chair of the Wisconsin Democrats.

I know how we’ve all been feeling lately – like there’s no check on what Donald Trump and Elon Musk are doing to our country. Like MAGA is all-powerful.

Peter, if you want to know where Trump and Musk’s real weakness lies, all you have to do is _follow the money._

**Elon Musk has already dropped _MILLIONS_ of dollars to bankroll Brad Schimel’s Supreme Court campaign here in Wisconsin**, because Musk and Trump know that Wisconsin’s highest court stands as a check on their lawless coup – and they know that extremist Republican Brad Schimel will be nothing but a rubber-stamp on their assault on constitutional checks and balances.

**That’s why we’re launching The People v. Musk – our official push to spread awareness about Musk’s hostile takeover of the Wisconsin Supreme Court and raise enough grassroots funding to fight back against his massive ad buys.**

[_**Will you split a $25 donation with Fight for Progress to help defeat Elon Musk, Donald Trump, and Brad Schimel, and keep Wisconsin OUT of the hands of right-wing oligarchs?**_](https://fight4progress.org/wisdems?t=DAZtrrVbMcvy&refcode=BLU_EM_FFP_2025-03-27_1&amount=25)
---
| | | [ CONTRIBUTE $25 ](https://fight4progress.org/wisdems?t=l6eXeUlxnivB&refcode=BLU_EM_FFP_2025-03-27_1&amount=25)

Elon Musk and Donald Trump want a MAGA Supreme Court to ban abortion with no exceptions for rape or incest; to overturn elections when they don’t like the results; and to suppress voters that don’t kiss their ring.

But we’re not going to let them buy this election. With enough grassroots support from folks like you, we’ll be able to kick our organizing operation into overdrive, ensure voters learn about the stakes on April 1, reject Elon Musk’s hostile takeover of our Supreme Court, and elect a true champion for fairness and democracy, Judge Susan Crawford.

[_**So I’m asking you, Peter, will you split a $25 donation with Fight for Progress right now to win the battle between we, the People, and Elon Musk and secure our pro-freedom majority?**_](https://fight4progress.org/wisdems?t=a2DGlzsALwej&refcode=BLU_EM_FFP_2025-03-27_1&amount=25)

# Democrats maintain PA House majority and flip red senate district!
---
This week the democratic majority control in the PA House of Representatives was up for grabs and all hinged on the 35th House District in Allegheny County in western PA. Democrat Dan Goughnour won the election maintaining the razor thin [democratic House majority](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMUG2YRxE5Jo0Xg1h2DyjzbycAoLNYnIOagLUoqqWrJ4FxkNijRePF5Mz6krXHj7l3AJbuVcy8SI-9_t-nQxoWO-Jq1jf_AkR54buaVt26FVNqpMb83MJi7CAhLOp2OEeSAQ9wnPgC8VuPMuKRkMEQXhYeN-p10YzBeaLubAlZ5ySDlenx-fy3j6rzrGWXC0oKdbN89U3TFbeOkk7Y88vqxJ_qim6ttYXjC3ngYulKyHFoRDPhcLqGmZLFoEMpC1nbQywgWXAQWgI-WAv_0SqhpAZD5J3pBicC9tFzWUPmU2COSYjWICu-3DCOtb6dgHSi28plYM6oSly4x74ukDwpW5d6jf8MND614yNao0c3VNnh8qpavrbHsMcZhqr3XvONA/4f6/BU547JKhT-u7QjQy0GjvDg/h1/h001.YmhGXtRTSfjAs6DmAfW2Tr5hC7FxeKbYKr0OD9p1I2o) of 102-101 majority! The seat was vacated in January upon the death of democratic Rep. Matthew Gergely. The eastern side of the state saw its own incredible shake-up as democrat James Malone won a PA senate seat in the 36th Senate District. This is a district that Trump won by +15 points and a seat that has not been held by a democrat since 1879. The seat was left open when Sen. Ryan Aument resigned to work for the US Sen. Dave McCormick. While the republicans will still maintain majority control of the PA Senate, it is now more narrow at 27-23 seats.

# Classified info, unforced errors, and the price we pay

In this week's edition of "WTF is going on with our federal government?" TLDR: Trump's national security adviser Mike Waltz used the [Signal app to discuss highly classified military strike plans](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMcDAEdtpGohpAzdSKj4-FXr46RkXezOQtLtG4B3LzpvRbqvKm_DpFZzv7lgzm--iIQHIAepIfGaxj9MMmsb8Cn_6Xgt6NtQ5RBxPYECFlYvaLAUZODcfDcsoEFIHbHbQJ1RQbS8wieDIU3XHSRrS-U8TN9dBtLmmI0PsIZ3ji2-q6h74pLtlcYMzt5Uhr-_vr4L5jO6F2bNv-r4n4n5A86HpF2lMm_bVNTvJmdXCcbh_z8QP-riRJct1SCSGIrOjZ01qy9qpHTO7sLwNLxAu4wWLQiBXmseeOPsG1pPmeLM-3dSl1QWkvVjgTsOUO7WD65ZdQfSPIybPQSpe3tTJnga9Fthd5huCx5hbDIgYlelr/4f6/BU547JKhT-u7QjQy0GjvDg/h3/h001.j9tbkN1rbRULLHnICNvnj9Lh4d_RtfjOSoRF6nGJTtg)**** on Yemen and, apparently accidentally, **added Atlantic editor in chief Jeffrey Goldberg****to the text**. Using a messaging app to communicate about classified information is a violation of Pentagon regulations, increases the risk of leaks, and puts all of our safety at risk. The text thread included top US officials, including Vice President JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
This type of inept mistake would ordinarily "prompt an investigation by the FBI and the Justice Department's national security division, according to former Justice Department officials. That's [unlikely here](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMcDAEdtpGohpAzdSKj4-FXr46RkXezOQtLtG4B3LzpvRbqvKm_DpFZzv7lgzm--iIQHIAepIfGaxj9MMmsb8Cn_6Xgt6NtQ5RBxPYECFlYvameyaqT_wYOy2DV5M-yW6W0TnTXRM-vydfInDVTjw-Q63pCOE43Nj3JM17Yduw2RXQHdfZBGwfp4XRqs_Rdqh5wwZy7BTeQcLXjCina84tBPY1jnN24VQ490LSuk-XryuedadNW15cGBIJ7o7H4j6UPyvkmvrjslWNAj00BoPXd2qbLn10Fg6kc-CvkKvYxwF--_6VK-DebDFRY3UiXav1dIaGvR5nZIRlsUwHky1FqcSPIU9-3zaCLeRAsmwfiMD/4f6/BU547JKhT-u7QjQy0GjvDg/h4/h001.gSGksxmvmKCWtu3-2MBt-hJYFzTPNYa09j4wVElSrqk), in part because some of the top Trump administration officials on the Signal chat would be the ones to ask for such an investigation." # DOJ Rescinds Key ADA Guidance
---
On Wednesday night, the Dept of Justice (DOJ) removed important guidance on accessibility in businesses, hotels, gas stations, regarding service animals, and more. While this doesn't materially change the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), by removing the guidelines it can become more challenging and confusing for businesses to comply and ensure accessibility. The federal agency in charge of reviewing guidance, US Access Board, had their meeting cancelled in January with no cause. The DOJ is charged with enforcing, not weakening, ADA protections. From confronting restrictive abortion policies to championing equity on the global stage, we are dedicated to creating a future where everyone has access to the health care they deserve. Our latest Annual Report highlights our impact over the last year—read it in this email. Here's a snapshot of our most recent efforts:

Thirty years ago, the United Nations adopted the **Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action** , a bold agenda for advancing women's rights. At the 69th session of the Commission on the Status of Women (CSW) March 10–21, 2025, in New York, global leaders assessed progress in sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) since 1995 and the challenges ahead.

To mark this milestone, we're sharing [**30 Years, 30 Stories**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/104672319/536129307/79158938?sourceid=1150552&utm_campaign=25emgfl-0301aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=frontlines&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiYmRlNTI4Ni1lNTBiLWYwMTEtOTBjZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=DSGSCDt-fpw7RPeDOiptohsofVl8m9ZQM6W65y12ibo=&emci=f155608c-8d06-f011-90cd-0022482a9fb7&emdi=bbde5286-e50b-f011-90cd-0022482a9fb7&ceid=954237), highlighting key gains in maternal health care, abortion access, gender equality, and human rights across Africa, Asia, Europe, and Latin America.

The Center for Reproductive Rights' discussions at CSW reinforced our commitment to making the promise of the Beijing Platform a reality:
* At _Daring to Deliver: Ensuring SRHR for Adolescents_ , **Enid Muthoni Ndiga** , Chief Program Officer at the Center, moderated a discussion on barriers adolescents face in exercising their SRHR, and the importance of comprehensive sexuality education
* In _Equality and Non-Discrimination for the Next 30 Years_ , **Katrine Thomasen** , Associate Director for Europe at the Center, joined a panel on gender equality, abortion rights, and conscientious objection.
* _From Beijing to Belém do Pará_ featured **Catalina Martínez Coral** , Vice President for Latin America and the Caribbean at the Center, alongside other global leaders reflecting on efforts to combat gender-based violence. Catalina also moderated _From Silence to Justice_ , which showcased legal victories against sexual violence and forced pregnancies in Latin America.

We're proud to share our [**2024 Annual Report**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/104672328/536129355/79158938?sourceid=1150552&utm_campaign=25emgfl-0301aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=frontlines&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiYmRlNTI4Ni1lNTBiLWYwMTEtOTBjZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=DSGSCDt-fpw7RPeDOiptohsofVl8m9ZQM6W65y12ibo=&emci=f155608c-8d06-f011-90cd-0022482a9fb7&emdi=bbde5286-e50b-f011-90cd-0022482a9fb7&ceid=954237), showcasing the impact we achieved together over the past year. **Your dedication makes this work possible.** As we push back against an emboldened opposition and advance reproductive autonomy worldwide, the power of law remains a potent tool. New research from the [**Institute for Women's Policy Research**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/104672339/536129383/-105093247?sourceid=1150552&utm_campaign=25emgfl-0301aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=frontlines&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiYmRlNTI4Ni1lNTBiLWYwMTEtOTBjZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=DSGSCDt-fpw7RPeDOiptohsofVl8m9ZQM6W65y12ibo=&emci=f155608c-8d06-f011-90cd-0022482a9fb7&emdi=bbde5286-e50b-f011-90cd-0022482a9fb7&ceid=954237) in collaboration with the Center for Reproductive Rights confirmed that access to reproductive health care is playing a key role in employee recruitment and retention. [**Most workers want employer-covered reproductive health benefits—and many are willing to relocate to secure them.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/104672340/536129386/-105093247?sourceid=1150552&utm_campaign=25emgfl-0301aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=frontlines&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiYmRlNTI4Ni1lNTBiLWYwMTEtOTBjZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=DSGSCDt-fpw7RPeDOiptohsofVl8m9ZQM6W65y12ibo=&emci=f155608c-8d06-f011-90cd-0022482a9fb7&emdi=bbde5286-e50b-f011-90cd-0022482a9fb7&ceid=954237)

Earlier this month in Austin, Texas, this critical issue took center stage at the South by Southwest Conference (SXSW) during the _Reproductive Freedom: Good for Workers, Good for Business_ panel featuring our President & CEO, Nancy Northup, alongside Dr. Chelsea Clinton and other leaders. They discussed the shifting legal landscape, strategies for businesses to navigate policies, and how local leaders are fighting to protect reproductive rights.

Rachana Desai Martin, our Chief Government & External Relations Officer, spoke on _Protecting Reproductive Freedom: What Leaders and Companies Must Do Now_ , highlighting corporate advocacy efforts like _Don't Ban Equality_.

Julia Taylor Kennedy, our Senior Director of Corporate Engagement, explored AI’s impact on women’s health care and its intersection with reproductive rights on a separate panel.
